subsystems.name: Block encoding
subsystems.role: embeds the non-unitary input matrix into a larger unitary so its singular values appear as a diagonal block.

subsystems.name: Polynomial approximation
subsystems.role: finds a polynomial that approximates the desired matrix function (e.g. inverse, exponential) to a required precision.

subsystems.name: Quantum signal processing (QSP) phase sequence
subsystems.role: the alternating single-qubit rotations that apply the polynomial to the block-encoded matrix.

subsystems.name: Quantum circuit
subsystems.role: the concrete gate sequence that implements block encoding and the QSP phase sequence on a quantum processor.

subsystems.name: Fault tolerance and error correction
subsystems.role: keeps the deep, high-precision circuit reliable enough for a useful result.

buildSteps.title: Define the target function
buildSteps.detail: Choose the matrix function to compute (for example, matrix inversion or Hamiltonian simulation) and the allowed error.

buildSteps.title: Approximate with a polynomial
buildSteps.detail: Use classical numerical methods to find a polynomial that matches the target function on the relevant interval to the desired accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Compute QSP phase angles
buildSteps.detail: Run a classical algorithm that converts the polynomial coefficients into a sequence of phase angles for the QSP circuit.

buildSteps.title: Build a block encoding
buildSteps.detail: Construct a unitary circuit that embeds the input matrix as a block, using ancilla qubits and controlled operations.

buildSteps.title: Compile the QSP sequence
buildSteps.detail: Translate the alternating rotations and controlled block-encoding steps into native gates for the target quantum hardware.

buildSteps.title: Prepare input and ancilla
buildSteps.detail: Initialise the data register in the desired input state and the ancilla in a known state.

buildSteps.title: Run and post-select
buildSteps.detail: Execute the circuit, measure the ancilla, and keep only runs where the ancilla indicates success.

buildSteps.title: Boost success probability
buildSteps.detail: If the success probability is low, apply amplitude amplification or a related technique to increase it.

buildSteps.title: Validate and estimate resources
buildSteps.detail: Check the output against classical simulation for small cases and estimate the qubit and gate counts needed for larger problems.

prerequisites.why: QSVT circuits for useful problems require thousands to millions of error-corrected qubits and deep gate sequences.
Several methods (e.g. linear combinations of unitaries, sparse access) exist in theory and small demonstrations, but resource costs remain high.
The theory is well developed and small-scale experiments on a few qubits have validated the basic principle.
Finding near-optimal polynomial approximations is a solved classical problem and is essential for setting the QSP phase angles.
Current hardware error rates are too high for the deep circuits QSVT demands without error correction.
Small codes have been demonstrated, but scaling to the required logical qubit counts and fidelities is still a major challenge.

pathway.milestone: QSVT and QSP validated on 2–3 qubit systems and used to unify known quantum algorithms theoretically
pathway.unlocks: confidence in the mathematical framework and a target for hardware development

pathway.milestone: precise resource estimates for practical applications such as linear systems and quantum chemistry
pathway.unlocks: clear specifications for the fault-tolerant quantum computers that would run QSVT

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant demonstrations of QSVT for small problem instances
pathway.unlocks: proof that the full pipeline works end-to-end with error correction

pathway.milestone: large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers running QSVT for real-world problems
pathway.unlocks: broad quantum speedups in simulation, optimisation and machine learning
